tier_rationale: The derivation of get–get from get–put and put–get is published (Kidney–Yang–Wu 2024, with a proof in the authors' Agda repository; Matache et al. 2025; Hillerström 2021); restated here for models on arbitrary carriers.
plain_claim: For every cell type S, every carrier X and every model M : Model S X, if M satisfies get–put and put–get as equations in X, then M satisfies get–get as an equation in X.

hypotheses.name: hGP : GetPut M
hypotheses.purpose: Gives x = M.get (fun t => M.put t x) for every x : X, which places a write of the value just read in front of both sides of get–get.
hypotheses.witness_class: a model on a Boolean cell with Boolean results (faultingCounter: counts reads, every write faults) satisfying put–get

hypotheses.name: hPG : PutGet M
hypotheses.purpose: Resolves the reads after that inserted write to the written value, collapsing both sides to M.get (fun t => M.put t (k t t)).
hypotheses.witness_class: a model on a Boolean cell with Boolean results (readToClear: reading resets the cell to false) satisfying get–put

nonvacuity_witness: inertHidden Bool Bool Bool (an ordinary cell next to an untouched hidden component) satisfies get–put and put–get.
non_claims: Concerns strict satisfaction (laws as equations in the carrier, for arbitrary carrier elements as continuations). Satisfaction through an observation (GetGetVia, GetPutVia, PutGetVia, PutPutVia) is a different notion: through a non-injective observation the strict entailments need not hold (getGetVia_not_entailed_by_getPutVia_putGetVia).
Does not say get–get follows from either law alone: each hypothesis is tight on a Boolean cell (getGet_of_tight_getPut, getGet_of_tight_putGet).

Does not say get–get is redundant together with put–put and one of the other two laws: getGet_not_entailed_by_pairs_with_putPut_bool gives Boolean-cell models of {get–put, put–put} and of {put–get, put–put} violating get–get.
The syntactic counterpart, derivability of every get–get instance from get–put and put–get instances, is the supporting lemma Derivable.getGet_of.

Models here take get and put with explicit continuations. For a monadic interface (get : m S, put : S → m Unit) the translation to these models relies on the monad laws (see the modeling bridge under Applicability); monads that violate them are not examined.
Concerns one cell; laws relating reads of different locations in multi-location state are not examined.

Model–system relation: none proved. These are statements about the toy model (one cell, free program syntax, set-like carriers); they neither establish nor refute the corresponding claims about any concrete language, library, device or verification tool.

design_question: When an interface is specified by the four state laws, which of them must be stated and checked? tier_rationale: Normal forms for global state are standard (see prior art).
plain_claim: For every cell type S, result type V and law set L containing get–put, put–get and put–put, every program p : Prog S V is derivable from L to be equal to get (fun s => put (run p s).2 (ret (run p s).1)), the canonical program of its intended observation run p.

hypotheses.name: hGP : L .getPut
hypotheses.purpose: Introduces the leading read for returns (ret v = get (fun s => put s (ret v))) and removes a read whose continuation ignores the value.
hypotheses.witness_class: L = all laws but get–put, Boolean cell, Boolean results, p = ret true

hypotheses.name: hPG : L .putGet
hypotheses.purpose: Resolves a read after a write (put t (get k) = put t (k t)); with get–put also derives get–get.
hypotheses.witness_class: L = all laws but put–get, Boolean cell, Boolean results, p = put true (get ret)

hypotheses.name: hPP : L .putPut
hypotheses.purpose: Merges consecutive writes into the last one.
hypotheses.witness_class: L = all laws but put–put, Boolean cell, Boolean results, p = put true (put false (ret true))

nonvacuity_witness: L = lawsExcept .getGet (get–put, put–get, put–put without get–get) satisfies all three hypotheses.
non_claims: Does not require get–get in L; it is derivable from get–put and put–get (Derivable.getGet_of), and including it is harmless.

Normal forms are relative to the free-monad syntax Prog, where the monad laws hold as literal equalities of programs; a syntax with an explicit bind constructor (where monad laws are extra axioms) is not covered.

Derivable contains the congruence rule get_congr with one premise per value of S; for infinite S this is an infinitary proof system (as with the infinitary lookup operation of Plotkin–Power), and the theorem gives no decision procedure for derivability.

Prog.get takes an arbitrary Lean function S → Prog S V as its continuation, and the canonical program nf (run p) uses arbitrary functions S → S and S → V. In a programming language whose programs are finitary syntax these functions need not be definable, so the theorem says nothing about normal forms within such a syntax.
Establishes that a derivation exists in the equational relation Derivable L; it is not a terminating or confluent rewrite system and gives no normalization algorithm.

plain_claim: For every cell type S, result type V and law set L, if canon f g and canon f' g' are derivably equal from L, then f = f' and g = g'.

hypotheses.name: h : Derivable L (canon f g) (canon f' g')
hypotheses.purpose: The premise; it transfers to equality of intended observations by soundness (the intended model satisfies every law).
hypotheses.witness_class: S = V = Bool: write maps fun s => s and fun s => !s, result maps both fun s => s; without the premise the conclusion fails for these maps

nonvacuity_witness: Reflexivity: Derivable allLaws (canon (fun s => !s) (fun s => s)) (canon (fun s => !s) (fun s => s)).

design_question: Is reasoning with the laws complete for the intended semantics? For one cell, yes: every observationally equivalent pair (same final value and final cell content from every initial content, ObsEq) is derivably equal from any law set containing get–put, put–get and put–put.

tier_rationale: A consequence of freeness of the state monad (Plotkin–Power).
plain_claim: For every model M on a carrier X satisfying get–put, put–get and put–put as equations in X, every valuation ρ : V → X and every program p, M.interp ρ p = M.get (fun s => M.put (run p s).2 (ρ (run p s).1)); that is, the interpretation of p in M is determined by its intended observation run p and by ρ.

hypotheses.name: hGP : GetPut M
hypotheses.purpose: Used through normal-form existence and soundness.
hypotheses.witness_class: dirtyBit on a Boolean cell with Boolean results (satisfies put–get, put–put)

hypotheses.name: hPG : PutGet M
hypotheses.purpose: Used through normal-form existence and soundness.
hypotheses.witness_class: writesIgnored on a Boolean cell with Boolean results (satisfies get–put, put–put)

hypotheses.name: hPP : PutPut M
hypotheses.purpose: Used through normal-form existence and soundness.
hypotheses.witness_class: changeLog on a Boolean cell with Boolean results (satisfies get–put, put–get)

nonvacuity_witness: inertHidden Bool Bool Bool satisfies get–put, put–get and put–put.
non_claims: Weakening strict satisfaction to satisfaction through a non-injective observation defeats the factorization: the write log satisfies all four laws through dropLog and distinguishes observationally equivalent programs (writeLog_via_distinguishes_obsEq).
Does not say the factor map is injective: at a fixed valuation, lawful models may identify different observations (valueOnly_lawful_not_faithful, unitModel_lawful_not_faithful).
The factorization is per valuation ρ; how M.interp depends on ρ is not constrained beyond this formula.

Does not exclude effects carried by the valuation: the strictly lawful intended model with results Bool × List Bool records a log supplied by the valuation (intended_leafLog_lawful_and_logs), and the strictly lawful inertHidden model changes its hidden component under the valuation pairFlipRet (inertHidden_pairFlipRet_changes_hidden). The laws constrain get and put; how these toy models relate to monad transformers such as a state monad over a writer monad is not proved here.

plain_claim: For every cell type S, result type V and programs p₀, q₀ : Prog S V such that p₀ = q₀ is not derivable from the four laws, the theory generated by the four laws together with every substitution instance p₀.bind σ = q₀.bind σ (σ : V → Prog S V) equates every two programs of type Prog S V.

hypotheses.purpose: Excludes adding an equation already in the theory.

nonvacuity_witness: p₀ = ret true, q₀ = ret false (S = V = Bool) is not derivable.
non_claims: 'Collapse' means: all programs of the fixed type Prog S V are identified, including ret v₁ = ret v₂ when V has two values. For a one-element result type it identifies programs that differ in their final cell content; there are no distinct return values to identify. Theories spanning several result types are not formalized.

Closure under substitution is built into the extended theory (rule ExtDerivable.inst). Without it the extension need not collapse: adding ret true = ret false alone (ExtDerivableNoSubst) does not identify put true (ret true) with put false (ret true) (extDerivableNoSubst_not_total).

The proof uses classical logic: it builds a continuation that branches on whether the cell holds a given value and a substitution that branches on equality of returned values. Prog.get accepts arbitrary Lean functions as continuations; whether the result holds for a syntax restricted to computable or finitary continuations, or constructively without decidable equality on S and V, is not examined.

Does not contradict valueOnly_lawful_not_faithful: valueOnly Bool Bool validates put true (ret true) = put false (ret true) under the valuation valueOnlyRet but not under the valuation fun _ s => s, and not for the substitution instance with get ret in place of each returned value (valueOnly_separates_other_valuation_and_substitution), so it is not a model of the theory extended by that equation.

On an empty cell, and on a one-element cell with one-element results, every two programs are already derivably equal (empty_cell_all_derivable, unit_cell_unit_result_all_derivable), so the hypothesis cannot be met there.
Concerns extensions by equations between programs. Extensions by inequations, conditional equations, new operations, or several cells are not examined.

non_claims: Preservation of the hidden component depends on the valuation pairRet: under pairFlipRet the same strictly lawful model changes the hidden component (inertHidden_pairFlipRet_changes_hidden).

prior_art: Constant-complement / product-state construction; elementary.
design_question: Is hidden state per se excluded by the laws? No: hidden state is compatible with all four laws even strictly. In inertHidden under pairRet, programs neither observe nor change it; under other valuations, or in other strictly lawful models, it can change, but never in a way that distinguishes observationally equivalent programs (interp_eq_of_obsEq_of_getPut_putGet_putPut).

tier_rationale: The derivation of get–get from get–put and put–get is published (see prior art).
plain_claim: For every cell type S, result type V and programs p, q : Prog S V, p = q is derivable from get–put, put–get and put–put iff it is derivable from all four laws.
nonvacuity_witness: Both sides are inhabited: a get–get instance is derivable from the laws other than get–get, and ret true = ret false is derivable from neither (Boolean cell).
non_claims: Does not say any other law can be dropped from the four: on a Boolean cell, dropping get–put, put–get or put–put loses equations (dropGetPut_loses_nf, dropPutGet_loses_nf, dropPutPut_loses_nf).

Dropping get–get is harmless when get–put and put–get are both present. It is not harmless from {get–get, get–put, put–put} or {get–get, put–get, put–put}: on a Boolean cell, a get–get instance is derivable neither from {get–put, put–put} nor from {put–get, put–put} (getGet_not_derivable_from_getPut_putPut, getGet_not_derivable_from_putGet_putPut).

Model–system relation: none proved. These are statements about the toy model (one cell, free program syntax, set-like carriers); they neither establish nor refute the corresponding claims about any concrete language, library, device or verification tool.
prior_art: D. O. Kidney, Z. Yang and N. Wu, 'Algebraic Effects Meet Hoare Logic in Cubical Agda', Proc. ACM Program. Lang. 8 (POPL), Article 56, 2024, DOI 10.1145/3632898. Section 3, Eq. (12): the theory of mutable state with the three laws put–put, put–get, get–put; the text states that get–get 'in fact follows from the equations above'. The authors' public Agda repository (github.com/oisdk/algebraic-free-monads-agda at commit 09f6fa1e9304732acfc72b4f8f2b9a52756361de, file Effects/State.agda) contains a proof of get–get from put–get and get–put (observed in the source; not type-checked here).

C. Matache, S. Lindley, S. K. Moss, S. Staton, N. Wu and Z. Yang, 'Scoped Effects, Scoped Operations, and Parameterized Algebraic Theories', ACM Trans. Program. Lang. Syst. 47(2), Article 8, 2025, DOI 10.1145/3731678 (earlier preprint, the extended version of the ESOP 2024 paper, as 'Scoped Effects as Parameterized Algebraic Theories', arXiv:2402.03103). Example 2.8: for the state of a single bit, with equations for put–get, put–put and get–put, 'the conspicuously missing equation for a get after a get ... can be derived', followed by a five-step derivation.

D. Hillerström, 'Foundations for Programming and Implementing Effect Handlers', PhD thesis, The University of Edinburgh, 2021; Edinburgh Research Archive record (dated 2022), DOI 10.7488/era/2122, handle 1842/38868 (author's copy, to which the page numbers below refer: dhil.net/research/papers/thesis.pdf). Section 1.2.2 (pp. 9-10) remarks that get–get is derivable from get–put and put–get; Appendix B ('Get get is redundant', p. 271) gives the derivation.
design_question: Dropping get–get from the four laws changes no derivable equation; it is a derived law.

tier_rationale: Folklore-level; the specific non-derivability witnesses and a mechanization were not located in the sources checked.
plain_claim: For a Boolean cell with Boolean results: from the laws other than get–put, ret true is not derivably equal to its canonical program get (fun s => put s (ret true)); from the laws other than put–get, put true (get ret) is not derivably equal to its canonical program; from the laws other than put–put, put true (put false (ret true)) is not derivably equal to its canonical program; in each case the two programs are observationally equivalent.
nonvacuity_witness: Closed statements (no hypotheses).
non_claims: Each non-derivability is shown by soundness in one model of the remaining three laws (dirtyBit, writesIgnored, changeLog respectively); other pairs of programs lost by dropping a law are not enumerated.

Proved for S = V = Bool. On a one-element cell the model-level independence behind these witnesses fails (unit_cell_putPut_of_getPut_putGet, unit_cell_lawful_of_getPut_putPut); whether the syntactic non-derivability results hold on other cell types is not examined.

Model–system relation: none proved. These are statements about the toy model (one cell, free program syntax, set-like carriers); they neither establish nor refute the corresponding claims about any concrete language, library, device or verification tool.
prior_art: Not located as stated results; elementary.
design_question: On a Boolean cell, each of get–put, put–get and put–put is tight for the normal-form and completeness theorems: without it, an observationally equivalent pair is not derivably equal.
